To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lysosomes contain dense bodies and that dense bodies contain electron-dense granular structures.
dense bodies, 0.37-µ in length, are found in lysosome-rich liver fractions, are also seen in electron micrographs from liver sections and may be identical to lysosomes.
lysosomal fractions from rat liver contain cytoplasmic structures that are not lysosomes, but are called "dense bodies."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the chemical and physical nature of the dense bodies.
the study of the submicroscopic morphology of liver cells.
the elucidation of the nature and origin of dense bodies and lysosomal particles in liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dense bodies are probably lysosomes.
dense bodies are a component of the lysosomal system.
dense bodies are lysosomes, and that lysosomes are dense bodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lysosome is a complex organelle which contains a number of enzymes capable of degrading a variety of substances and which, in addition, possesses a variety of cytoplasmic constituents, including dense bodies, which may have a role in lysosomal function.
the lysosome-rich fraction contains, in addition to lysosomes, other particles which may be related to the dense bodies.
dense bodies and the lysosomes of liver cells appear to be identical, or at least closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dense bodies are a new type of organelle that may be related to lysosomes.
the dense bodies and the lysosomes are not identical, but that both are derived from the same precursor organelle.
dense bodies and other particles in the cytoplasm are not necessarily artifacts of preparation, but may be normal components of the cell.
